subject: Fee stabilization language in pricing exhibit — carry-forward & packaging credits
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir@helixhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on 'stabilization buffer' in Exhibit B

Jonas —

Thanks for the draft. We were reviewing Exhibit B and want to confirm how the "Fee Stabilization Buffer" interacts with packaging credits and the monthly cap language. Two quick items: 

1) If usage drops below the monthly committed threshold and we earn packaging credits, can Helix carry those credits forward and apply them against subsequent months that exceed the commit? Or are credits limited to the month they are earned?

2) The pricing exhibit references a "monthly cap" for credits but doesn't say whether the cap is applied before or after any floor/true-up. Practically that matters for our finance reconciliation.

I've attached a marked-up redline that shows Helix's preferred treatment (carry-forward allowed, 24-month shelf, monthly cap at 20% of monthly committed spend). Can you confirm Redwood's position? We're trying to lock the orderform this week.

Samir
Samir Desai
Head of Procurement, HelixHealth
samir@helixhealth.com

Subject: Re: Question on 'stabilization buffer' in Exhibit B

Samir —

Thanks for the markup. From a commercial standpoint here's a pragmatic approach that tends to work with finance teams:

Proposal (commercial):
- Allow earned packaging credits to be carried forward for up to 12 months from the month they are earned.
- Monthly credit application is capped at 15% of that month's committed spend (to preserve predictable revenue recognition).
- Credits do not reduce the monthly floor for true-up purposes; true-ups are calculated on gross usage before credits. Credits instead apply after the true-up calculation.

Rationale: the 12-month shelf balances Helix's request for flexibility with Redwood's need to close revenue in a timely fashion. The 15% cap limits the distortion in a single month. Applying credits after true-up keeps the unit economics transparent.

I've attached a short compare (pricing-exhibit-compare.pdf) showing how the math flows under the three models (no carry, 12-month carry at 15%, Helix-marked 24-month at 20%). Happy to move to legal redline once you confirm you can live with 12 months / 15%.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'stabilization buffer' in Exhibit B

All —

Please find below a tight legal redline we can insert into Exhibit B. I've kept it short and referenced defined terms already in the orderform.

Suggested redline (to insert under "Fee Stabilization & Credits"):
"Earned Packaging Credits may, at Customer's election, be carried forward and applied against future invoices for up to twelve (12) months from the month in which such Credits were earned. For the avoidance of doubt, Credits shall be applied after any Monthly True‑Up calculation and shall not reduce the Monthly Commitment amount used to determine whether a True‑Up is owed. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Credits applied in any single invoice period shall not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the Monthly Commitment for such invoice period. Any unused Credits remaining after the twelve (12) month carry‑forward window shall expire without liability to Provider."
Key legal considerations:
- Preserve the defined term "Monthly Commitment" so true-ups remain calculable on grosss usage.
- Cap at 15% to limit revenue leakage.
- Explicitly state expiration to avoid open-ended liability.

If you're good, I'll prepare a redline doc for the orderform and include an implementation note for billing to ensure credits hit post-true-up. Let me know if Helix pushes for a longer shelf — we can trade shelf length for a slightly lower cap.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Samir Desai <samir@helixhealth.com>

Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'stabilization buffer' in Exhibit B

Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear language. Helix can accept the 12-month shelf, but we'd like to request a small modification: increase the per-invoice cap to 25% (from 15%) if Helix provides a rolling 12-month forecast that meets minimum commit targets. That gives our finance team runway to smooth usage without creating a large one-off offset.

If Redwood can accept the conditional 25% cap (forecast to be delivered monthly), we can proceed and aim to sign the orderform this week. Otherwise we will accept the 15% cap but request an additional true-up reporting cadence (weekly usage export) for the first 90 days.

Happy to sign if you can add the DocuSign route.

Best,
Samir
Samir Desai
Head of Procurement, HelixHealth
samir@helixhealth.com
